name: Packet duplication to secondary APIDs (inferred title)
purpose: Inferred from the data; not documented in any available ICD. Each record links one SCOS-2000 TM packet definition (column 1, a PID_SPID) to a second APID (column 2) in the range 1953-1996. These APIDs do not belong to on-board applications in this MIB: for each of the 41 distinct values the pid table holds many finer packet definitions with the same type/subtype, and the pic table holds a record keyed by that APID (PIC_APID) that places the second identification field PI2 (or PI1) deeper inside the packet. Example: SPID 14177 'On-board Parameters Value Report' (TM(139,3) from APID 163, no extra identification field) maps to APID 1953, where PIC defines a 32-bit PI1 at byte 17 and pid defines 20 specific reports (e.g. 'FSS Thresholds Value Report'). This suggests a ground mechanism that copies (duplicates) generic packets such as event reports (5,x), memory dumps (6,6), monitoring reports (12,9) or parameter reports under a ground-only APID, so that SCOS-2000 can identify and decommutate each variant with its own SPID and layout. The mechanism itself is not described in the available sources.

fields.name: COL1
fields.description: Inferred: SCOS-2000 packet ID (SPID) of the original packet definition. All 69 values (2025 release) exist in pid.PID_SPID and are unique. The referenced packets are mostly PUS event reports (5,1), (5,2), (5,3) (38 rows), memory dumps (6,6) (11), and mission-specific report types 12/9, 131/2, 131/128, 132/2, 139/3, 141/3 and 142/11.

fields.name: COL2
fields.description: Inferred: the secondary (ground) APID under which the duplicated packet is identified again. 41 distinct values in 2025; several SPIDs can share one APID (e.g. 1961 for six memory-dump SPIDs). Every value has pid records (PID_APID) and pic records (PIC_APID) with the same type/subtype as the source packet but different PI1/PI2 offsets.

relationships.note: All 41 APIDs have APID-specific PIC records defining the secondary identification fields (inferred).
All APIDs have packet definitions; APIDs 1950-1999 carry 2,421 pid records in 2025.

history: Not part of any ICD issue (5.1, 6.7 Draft A, 6.9, 7.0) nor of the pyscos2000 (7.2) schema. 36 rows in MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL, 69 rows in MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL. Not present in the SWA instrument database.
notes: Meanings inferred from joins against pid and pic (2025 release). The pic precedence rules of ICD 7.0 section 3.3.2.4.2 (type/subtype/APID first, then type/subtype; PDF p.91-92) explain how an APID-specific PIC record changes the identification of a packet; how and where the duplication is performed is not stated in the available sources. The name 'dup' presumably abbreviates 'duplicate' (inference).
